metadata.title: Read a Text File
metadata.description: Read a seeded text file with a with-block and print its line count.

instructions.main: `names.txt` lives in the workspace. Read it and print how many lines it contains.
steps: Open the file from the workspace: `with open("names.txt") as f:`.
Print the count with `print(len(lines))` — for the seeded file the answer is `4`.

hints.message: Open `names.txt` with `with open("names.txt") as f:`, read its lines, then `print(len(lines))`.
Open files with `with open("names.txt") as f:` — a `with` block closes the file for you; a bare `open(...)` relies on garbage collection and can leak the handle.
Don't hardcode an absolute path — the file is right there in the workspace as `names.txt`. Use `open("names.txt")`.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: You read names.txt with a with-block and printed its line count.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Read all of `names.txt` and print the number of lines — for the seeded file it is `4`.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: You opened the file with a with-block.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Open the file with `with open("names.txt") as f:` — the with-statement closes the file automatically.
